research_period: Shows 10 September to 6 October 2026; Haute Couture, July 2026; Premiere Vision Paris, February 2026; analysis October to November 2026
markets: Global: New York, London, Milan, Paris and Copenhagen runways; premium and mid-market womenswear
title: SS27 Women's Trim Innovations
summary: Ribbon built into the cloth, coated and pearlescent lace, rubberised corsetry meshes and fastenings used as decoration: the newest trim ideas for SS27.

sections.heading: Ribbon as structure
sections.body: Première Vision describes ribbon acting as material, ornament and structure: finishing ribbons, highly decorative ribbons and ribbons integrated into fabric construction, inlaid into jacquards, embroidered as backgrounds or applied onto tulle and lace<sup>[1]</sup>. For production, this means trims ordered as part of the fabric rather than added at the end.

sections.heading: Coated and pearlescent lace
sections.body: The "Wet Sheen" direction brings plastic-coated laces and pearlescent satins<sup>[1]</sup>. Première Vision's decoration report adds Leavers lace with a melted-film coating for a latex-like sheen<sup>[2]</sup>. On the runway, Saint Laurent coated latex in gold leaf<sup>[3]</sup>.

sections.heading: Corsetry components
sections.body: Membrane-backed draperies, spacer fabrics and rubberised meshes borrowed from corsetry appear among Première Vision's structural fabrics<sup>[1]</sup>. They let a bodice hold its shape without boning.

sections.heading: Fastenings as decoration
sections.body: Prada used coloured Velcro strips with embroidered florals on the fastenings<sup>[4]</sup>; Ferragamo covered snap buttons in sequins<sup>[3]</sup>; Miu Miu laced skirts with cross-lace fastenings<sup>[4]</sup>; Givenchy made belt buckles that double as powder compacts<sup>[4]</sup>.

sections.heading: Readiness
sections.body:
| Innovation | Readiness for production (Forecut assessment) |
|---|---|
| Ribbon-inlaid jacquards | Available from specialist mills; long lead times |
| Coated and pearlescent lace | Available; test cleaning and abrasion |
| Rubberised and spacer meshes | Available from lingerie and sportswear suppliers |
| Decorative fastenings | Ready; mainly a design and sourcing decision |

design_implications:
- Bring trim suppliers into fabric development early when ribbon is part of the cloth.
- Test coated laces for cracking, peeling and dry-cleaning.
- Use corsetry meshes to shape bodices and bra tops without rigid boning.
commercial_implications:
- Innovative trims justify a premium on a few hero pieces; do not spread them across the range.
- Long lead times for jacquard ribbons mean early commitment: order SS27 quantities now and limit reorders.
